nodes.title: Matrix mortality
nodes.summary: Nonempty zero products in a finite family of integer matrices, with dimension and generator count fixed.

nodes.title: Word-pair representation
nodes.summary: A three-dimensional matrix morphism that records two ternary words and detects their equality in one coefficient.

nodes.title: Fixed-boundary correspondence
nodes.summary: Four nonerasing word pairs recognize restricted tag halting when the terminal marker is fixed rather than selectable.

nodes.title: Paired scalar series
nodes.summary: The four source roles are encoded by two data controls and one toggle; their four-dimensional scalar coefficient detects the decoded word equality.

nodes.title: Paired-role compression
nodes.summary: Two phase copies share an agreement subspace, replacing four linear actions by two data controls and a toggle.

nodes.title: Rank-one separator
nodes.summary: One repeated outer product turns a vanishing scalar coefficient into a matrix zero; the converse accounts for arbitrary products.

nodes.title: Interface compression
nodes.summary: Partitioning an ordinary generator family into transitions and factored cuts reduces its cut-containing products exactly to paths of interface bridges; transition-only products remain a separate branch.

nodes.title: Singular-return compression
nodes.summary: When no transition power vanishes, mortality of one transition and one cut is equivalent to mortality of their complete return family.

nodes.title: Six-dimensional scalar compiler
nodes.summary: Two-bit codewords select the four source roles. Sharing the unfinished upper-word coordinates gives two matrices in dimension six.

nodes.title: Generator packing
nodes.summary: A general alphabet reduction trades generator count for additional coordinate blocks, preserving mortality in both directions.

nodes.title: Binary prefix decoder
nodes.summary: A complete binary code represents the five source matrices on four three-dimensional decoder blocks; a synchronizing word handles every starting block.

nodes.title: Common-image restriction
nodes.summary: A decoder family is restricted to its common invariant image, with an appended-letter converse excluding new zero products.

nodes.title: Tilted separator
nodes.summary: An injective length-tilted ternary code changes the nonzero coefficients needed by the realization while preserving the complete zero language.

nodes.title: Nine-dimensional return realization
nodes.summary: Two length-three nilpotent chains, one length-two chain, and one eigenline realize three exceptional moments and a geometric tail.

nodes.title: Tilted-geometric rank floor
nodes.summary: One fixed source instance requires nine dimensions throughout the stated tilted geometric-tail family; the bound concerns exact realizations of those returns.

nodes.title: Effective denominator clearing
nodes.summary: Independent nonzero generator scalings convert a rational family to integer matrices while preserving and reflecting every zero product.

nodes.title: Valuation guard
nodes.summary: A three-mode return family forces one legal wait by a p-adic valuation and sends every wrong wait into a permanent trap.

nodes.title: Valuation barriers
nodes.summary: Parity and prime-divisibility conditions prove that specified guarded families have no zero product.

nodes.title: Two-generator projective incidence
nodes.summary: Given two invertible rational 2 × 2 matrices, a source column and a target row, ask whether some word moves the column into the row’s kernel.

nodes.title: Shortcut-Collatz reachability
nodes.summary: Finite reachability of 1 under halving on even integers and (3n+1)/2 on odd integers.

nodes.title: Shortcut-Collatz incidence
nodes.summary: Two fixed fractional-linear maps recognize exactly those supplied integers that reach 1 under shortcut Collatz, by a scalar-zero test.

nodes.title: Rank-two projective-incidence compiler
nodes.summary: Every generic two-generator projective-incidence instance compiles to two rational 3 × 3 matrices of rank exactly two, with mortality equivalent to incidence zero.

nodes.title: M₃(5) is undecidable
nodes.summary: Four fixed-boundary payload matrices and one repeated rank-one separator give five 3 × 3 integer matrices.

nodes.title: M₄(4) is undecidable
nodes.summary: Paired-role compression gives three 4 × 4 scalar controls; one rank-one separator converts their zero coefficient to mortality.

nodes.title: Z₆(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: The shared-partial compiler preserves the paired coefficient under every binary word in dimension six.

nodes.title: R₇(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: The scalar-to-corner transport converts the six-dimensional two-generator scalar theorem to a seven-dimensional corner theorem.

nodes.title: M₁₀(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: A complete binary prefix decoder followed by common-image restriction gives two 10 × 10 integer matrices.

nodes.title: M₉(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: A zero-language-equivalent separator and a nine-dimensional return realization give a primitive-recursive pair of integer matrices.

nodes.title: M₆(3) is undecidable
nodes.summary: Applying generator packing to M₃(5) gives M₆(3). This is a frontier bound, not a separate construction.

nodes.title: M₁₂(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: Applying generator packing to M₃(5) gives M₁₂(2). The bound is now subsumed by M₈(2).

nodes.title: Periodic-prefix exclusion
nodes.summary: The compiler's bcb prefix and lower-tile grammar exclude every competing capped period, ruling out all asymmetric wrong-phase zeros.

nodes.title: Asymmetric separator
nodes.summary: Only erase-phase equalities remain zero; a leading toggle recovers every discarded witness. Existence is preserved, not the pointwise zero language.

nodes.title: Eight-dimensional return realization
nodes.summary: Two length-three nilpotent chains, one static coordinate, and one eigenline realize a rescaled toggle, two data roles, and the asymmetric separator tail.

nodes.title: M₈(2) is undecidable
nodes.summary: Existential phase selection and an eight-dimensional return realization give a primitive-recursive pair of integer matrices, mortal exactly when its source program halts.

views.title: Foundations
views.summary: The mortality problem and the matrix language every construction is written in.

views.title: Source Recognition
views.summary: The undecidable source problem and the four-dimensional scalar series that later constructions reuse.

views.title: Target Compression
views.summary: Reductions that turn scalar or interface zeros into unrestricted matrix products.

views.title: Binary and Return Constructions
views.summary: Realizations that reach fewer generators or lower dimension, built on the source series and the interface reduction.

views.title: Arithmetic Incidence
views.summary: Where two-generator projective incidence meets arithmetic dynamics, including its shortcut-Collatz instance.

views.title: Established Obstructions
views.summary: Limits proved for specified constructions, not impossibility results for the unresolved table entries.

views.title: Frontier Constructions
views.summary: Constructions establishing current frontier bounds. Consequences obtained only by applying an existing transport are listed separately below.

views.title: Subsumed Constructions
views.summary: Mortality constructions whose endpoint now follows from a sharper frontier theorem, retained for their distinct mechanisms.

views.title: Transported Bounds
views.summary: Corollaries of existing packing or scalar-to-corner reductions, not separate constructions. A transported bound may still lie on the numerical frontier.
